context.what_changed: The feature lets a team credit people and organizations on a project, dataset, sample or measurement, and makes a level held on that credit (view, edit, manage) the only thing that decides who opens, changes and manages a record. It replaces the stored per-object permission rows (django-guardian) as the source of rights on core records with a level query: fairdm/contrib/contributors/access.py, permissions.py, services/crediting.py, fairdm/core/permissions.py, fairdm/core/managers.py, fairdm/utils/permissions.py, fairdm/api/permissions.py, fairdm/conf/settings/auth.py. Two migrations under fairdm/contrib/contributors/migrations/: 0022 (schema) and 0023 (converts stored permissions to levels; nobody may lose access on upgrade).

focus: Security lens only, per craft-security, with craft-review's method. This change replaces the permission backend, so the question is: can anyone now open, change, manage, list or learn of a record they could not before, or do so without the level the spec requires?

Walk every entry point to a core record and to its contributors: each view and plugin page (GET and POST), each form field (visibility and the parent field need manage), each queryset and manager (visible_to, with_level), each API viewset, serializer, filter and permission class, the list pages, search and autocomplete endpoints, and the ORCID/ROR registry lookups (outbound fetches: SSRF, identifier format checked before any request, timeouts, what is trusted from the response).

Object-level checks: IDOR across records (a contribution id from another record in the URL or the POST body), across subject types, and through the parent chain (project to dataset to sample to measurement). Does a level on a parent leak to or get denied on a child the way the spec says?
Anonymous users, signed-in users with no credit, view, edit, manage, portal staff, superuser: for each, the denied and absent states, and whether a denial reveals that a private record exists.

Privilege escalation: can an edit-level person raise their own level, add a manager, remove the last manager, move a record to a parent they do not manage, or merge profiles to inherit a level? Unclaimed profiles and account takeover: no email is collected on the by-hand person form (decision D19); check nothing else stores or matches an address that a password reset could use.

Migration 0023 from a security view: does anyone end with more than they had? Are stale guardian rows still honoured anywhere (settings AUTHENTICATION_BACKENDS, has_perm call sites, templates using perms)?
Mass assignment and CSRF on the new forms and API writes; unescaped output of names, affiliations and registry data in templates and JSON; logging of personal data.
Severity is reachable consequence from the package's real surface. A missing authorization check on a reachable page or endpoint is high or critical.
